title: Multi-Generation LLM Quality Degradation Analysis
assumption: LLMs can be iteratively trained on AI-generated content without quality loss
hypothesis: Iterative training on AI-generated outputs causes systematic performance degradation across reasoning, knowledge, and coding capabilities
evaluationPlan: 1. Establish baseline performance on 8 benchmark datasets (MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval, etc.) 2. Simulate 5 generations of iterative training 3. Measure degradation rates across capability domains 4. Statistical analysis of degradation patterns and correlations
implications: Would establish empirical evidence for model collapse theory and inform AI training best practices
relatedWork: Shumailov et al. (2023) - Model Collapse, AI-generated content detection literature, LLM benchmark studies
milestones: 1. Baseline evaluation complete 2. Generation 1-2 analysis 3. Generation 3-5 analysis 4. Statistical modeling 5. Results publication
successCriteria: Quantified degradation rates >10% per generation, capability hierarchy established, predictive models developed
notes: Comprehensive benchmark suite downloaded and ready for analysis

title: Capability-Specific Degradation Rate Analysis
assumption: All LLM capabilities degrade uniformly during iterative training
hypothesis: Mathematical reasoning and code generation degrade faster than factual knowledge retention
evaluationPlan: 1. Separate analysis of mathematical (GSM8K), coding (HumanEval/MBPP), and knowledge (MMLU/TruthfulQA) benchmarks 2. Statistical comparison of degradation rates 3. Correlation analysis between different capability domains
implications: Would inform targeted training strategies and capability-specific monitoring
relatedWork: Cognitive architecture literature, domain-specific LLM evaluation studies
milestones: 1. Capability domains defined 2. Separate degradation curves generated 3. Statistical significance testing 4. Hierarchy ranking
successCriteria: Statistically significant differences in degradation rates between capabilities (p<0.05)

title: Early Warning Indicator Detection
assumption: Performance degradation across benchmarks is unpredictable
hypothesis: Certain benchmarks serve as early warning indicators for broader model collapse
evaluationPlan: 1. Temporal analysis of benchmark performance changes 2. Lead-lag correlation analysis 3. Machine learning models to predict future degradation based on current metrics 4. Validation on held-out generation data
implications: Would enable proactive model health monitoring and intervention strategies
relatedWork: Time series analysis in ML, predictive maintenance literature
milestones: 1. Correlation matrices generated 2. Predictive models trained 3. Validation testing complete 4. Warning system prototype
successCriteria: Ability to predict degradation 1-2 generations in advance with >80% accuracy
notes: Requires completion of multi-generation experiment first

title: Large-Scale Multi-Model Architecture Validation
assumption: Digital inbreeding effects are model-specific rather than fundamental
hypothesis: Digital inbreeding effects are consistent across different model architectures and scales, suggesting fundamental rather than model-specific limitations
evaluationPlan: 1. Test across GPT-2 (124M, 355M, 774M), DistilBERT, RoBERTa architectures 2. 5 generations per model with gradual mixing ratios (10%, 30%, 50%, 70%, 90% synthetic) 3. 50 samples per condition (5x increase) 4. Full benchmark suite evaluation 5. Statistical power analysis for generalizability
implications: Would establish whether digital inbreeding is a fundamental AI limitation or model-specific artifact
relatedWork: Model scaling laws literature, architecture comparison studies, AI safety generalization research
milestones: 1. Multi-architecture baseline establishment 2. Cross-model degradation analysis 3. Architecture vulnerability ranking 4. Generalizability validation
successCriteria: Consistent degradation patterns across architectures (correlation > 0.7), statistically significant effects (p < 0.01) with medium+ effect sizes (Cohen's d > 0.5)
notes: First cross-architecture validation of digital inbreeding with enhanced statistical power

title: Temporal Dynamics and Decay Function Modeling
assumption: LLM performance degradation patterns are unpredictable
hypothesis: LLM performance degradation follows predictable mathematical functions that can be modeled and forecasted
evaluationPlan: 1. Extended to 10 training iterations with evaluation at 0.5 generation intervals 2. Fit linear, exponential, logarithmic, and sigmoid decay functions 3. Use early generations to predict later performance 4. 5-fold temporal cross-validation 5. Mathematical model development
implications: Would enable predictive modeling of model degradation and optimal training intervention timing
relatedWork: Mathematical modeling in ML, decay function analysis, time series forecasting in AI
milestones: 1. Extended generation data collection 2. Mathematical function fitting 3. Predictive model validation 4. Forecasting accuracy assessment
successCriteria: Mathematical model explains >80% of variance in degradation, predictions accurate within 5% for 2-generation forecasts
notes: First systematic modeling of degradation functions with predictive capability validation

title: Capability Hierarchy and Asymmetric Degradation
assumption: All cognitive capabilities degrade uniformly during iterative training
hypothesis: Different cognitive capabilities exhibit distinct vulnerability patterns to iterative training degradation, enabling construction of capability resilience hierarchy
evaluationPlan: 1. Domain separation: Mathematical reasoning (GSM8K, MATH), Code generation (HumanEval, MBPP), Factual knowledge (MMLU, TruthfulQA), Language understanding (SuperGLUE, WinoGrande), Creative generation (WritingPrompts) 2. Fine-grained sub-domain analysis 3. Cross-domain degradation correlations 4. Structural equation modeling of capability dependencies
implications: Would inform targeted training strategies and capability-specific monitoring protocols
relatedWork: Cognitive architecture literature, domain-specific LLM evaluation, capability transfer studies
milestones: 1. Capability domain definition and separation 2. Sub-domain degradation pattern identification 3. Vulnerability hierarchy establishment 4. Predictive cross-capability model development
successCriteria: Capability vulnerability hierarchy established with statistical significance, predictive model for cross-capability degradation developed
notes: First systematic mapping of capability-specific vulnerability patterns with causal analysis

title: Early Warning System Development
assumption: Model degradation cannot be predicted before it becomes apparent
hypothesis: Specific evaluation metrics serve as leading indicators for broader model collapse, enabling preventive intervention
evaluationPlan: 1. Lead-lag time series analysis across 20+ metrics 2. Machine learning models to predict degradation 3. Critical warning threshold identification 4. Early stopping and data filtering intervention testing 5. Real-time monitoring system development
implications: Would enable practical early warning systems for production AI model health monitoring
relatedWork: Predictive maintenance literature, time series analysis in ML, AI system monitoring
milestones: 1. Leading indicator identification 2. Predictive model training 3. Threshold determination 4. Intervention effectiveness validation
successCriteria: Warning system predicts degradation 1-2 generations in advance with >85% accuracy, clear intervention threshold identification
notes: First development of practical early warning system for model degradation

title: Information-Theoretic Mechanism Analysis
assumption: Digital inbreeding mechanisms are not well understood
hypothesis: Digital inbreeding reduces information entropy and mutual information between training generations, providing mechanistic understanding of degradation
evaluationPlan: 1. Entropy tracking: Shannon entropy, Rényi entropy, differential entropy 2. Mutual information analysis between generations, within domains, cross-domains 3. KL divergence tracking across generations 4. Information-theoretic degradation model development 5. Correlation validation with performance degradation
implications: Would provide theoretical foundation for understanding model collapse mechanisms
relatedWork: Information theory in ML, entropy analysis in AI, theoretical foundations of model collapse
milestones: 1. Comprehensive entropy analysis 2. Mutual information pattern identification 3. Mechanistic model development 4. Performance correlation validation
successCriteria: Clear entropy reduction patterns identified, mechanistic model explains >70% of performance variance
notes: First comprehensive information-theoretic analysis of model collapse mechanisms

title: Mitigation Strategy Evaluation
assumption: Digital inbreeding effects cannot be prevented or mitigated
hypothesis: Strategic interventions including data mixing, regularization, and architectural modifications can significantly reduce or prevent digital inbreeding effects
evaluationPlan: 1. Test intervention strategies: optimal data mixing ratios, regularization techniques (dropout, weight decay, noise injection), architectural modifications, training procedure adaptations 2. Head-to-head strategy comparison 3. Computational cost vs. degradation prevention analysis 4. Scalability testing across model sizes
implications: Would enable development of practical solutions to prevent model degradation in production systems
relatedWork: AI training optimization, regularization techniques, data curation strategies
milestones: 1. Intervention strategy implementation 2. Comparative effectiveness evaluation 3. Cost-benefit analysis 4. Scalable protocol development
successCriteria: Identification of strategies reducing degradation by >50%, cost-effective mitigation protocols established
notes: First systematic evaluation of practical mitigation strategies for digital inbreeding
